name: Ray-Box Intersection via OpenGL Geometry Shaders
definition: A method to compute the entry and exit points of rays (defined by camera projection) intersecting a bounding box (the volume) by rendering the box geometry to textures using OpenGL, storing the hit positions in 16-bit floating point textures.
summary: This method computes ray-box entry and exit points using a single-pass OpenGL geometry shader, avoiding complex CPU calculations and differing from two-pass alternatives.
